And isn't that decision itself a moral stance? I think it is. I think we're always bringing our own values and biases to the table when we try to create a neutral system.

Take our store's return policy, for example. We have a pretty straightforward policy, but it's not neutral. It's based on our values of customer satisfaction and fairness. We want to make sure customers are happy, so we have a pretty lenient return policy. But, if we were to change that policy, it would be because we've decided that our values have shifted, not because we've become more neutral.

And it's not just about policies, either. Even the way we design our store's layout is a moral stance. We choose to put the organic produce up front because we believe that's what our customers want. We're not just being neutral, we're making a choice that reflects our values.

So, I think neutrality is just a myth. We're always making moral choices, even when we think we're being neutral. And that's okay. I think it's okay to have values and to make decisions based on them. It's just important to be aware of them and to be honest with ourselves and our customers about what we're doing.

You know, I've been thinking about this a lot because of all the changes going on in the world. I feel like we're at a point where we have to be more intentional about our values and our choices. We can't just pretend like we're being neutral and expect everything to work out. We have to be willing to take a stand and make decisions that reflect our values.
